shm-representations-s1.title: Position of a cart on a spring
shm-representations-s1.text: A motion detector records the position of a cart oscillating on a horizontal spring on a frictionless track. Position is measured from equilibrium; + is to the right.

shm-representations-s2.title: An equation of motion
shm-representations-s2.text:
A block on a spring moves along a frictionless surface. Its position, measured from equilibrium in meters, is

x(t) = (0.040 m) sin(2π · 2.5 t)

with t in seconds. The calculator must be in radian mode for this equation.

items.q: What is the period of the cart's motion? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the time from one turning point to the other, half a cycle. A period ends when the cart is back at +0.15 m moving the same way.

why.correct: The cart is at +0.15 m at t = 0 and next at t = 0.80 s, so T = 0.80 s. Half a period (0.40 s) only takes it to the other side.

items.q: At which time is the cart moving fastest?

why.correct: Speed is the steepness of the position-time graph. The graph is steepest where it crosses x = 0, at t = 0.20 s (and 0.60 s, 1.00 s...). The cart passes equilibrium at top speed.
options: Right: the slope is steepest where x = 0.
At 0.40 s the cart is at −0.15 m, a turning point: the slope is zero and the cart is momentarily at rest.
At 0.80 s the cart is back at +0.15 m, a turning point with zero speed.
At 0.30 s the cart is between equilibrium and a turning point; it is still moving, but slower than at 0.20 s.

items.q: What are the directions of the cart's velocity and acceleration at t = 0.50 s?
options: Velocity +, acceleration +
Velocity −, acceleration +
Velocity +, acceleration −
Velocity −, acceleration −

why.correct: At 0.50 s the cart is below zero (x < 0) and the graph is rising, so v is +. The acceleration always points toward equilibrium, opposite to x; x is negative, so a is +.
options: Right: x < 0 and rising, so v > 0 and a = −(k/m)x > 0.
The graph is rising at 0.50 s (it left −0.15 m at 0.40 s), so the velocity is positive.
Acceleration is opposite to the displacement; with x negative, a is positive.
Both signs are off: the graph is rising at 0.50 s (v > 0), and with x below zero the acceleration points toward equilibrium (a > 0).

items.q: The cart is stopped and released again from x = +0.075 m. Which graph feature changes, compared with the graph shown?
options: The peaks are half as high, and the time between them is unchanged
The peaks are half as high, and the time between them is halved
The peaks are the same height, and the time between them is halved
The peaks are half as high, and the time between them is doubled

why.correct: Releasing from 0.075 m makes the amplitude 0.075 m, half of 0.15 m. The period T = 2π√(m/k) does not depend on the amplitude, so the peaks stay 0.80 s apart.
options: Right: smaller amplitude, same period.
A smaller amplitude does not shorten the period: less distance, but proportionally less force and speed.
The release point sets the amplitude, so the peaks must be lower.
The period depends on m and k only; amplitude does not lengthen it.

items.q: What is the period of the block's motion? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you multiplied 2π by the frequency. In x = A sin(2πft), the number multiplying 2πt is f = 2.5 Hz, and T = 1/f.
Value: 2.5 is the frequency in hertz. The period is T = 1/f.

why.correct: Compare with x = A sin(2πft): f = 2.5 Hz, so T = 1/f = 0.40 s.

items.q: What is the block's position at t = 0.050 s? Include the sign and the unit.

mistakes.why: Value: your calculator was in degree mode. The angle 2π(2.5)(0.050) = 0.785 is in radians.

why.correct: x = (0.040 m) sin(2π × 2.5 × 0.050) = (0.040 m) sin(0.785 rad) = (0.040 m)(0.707) = 0.028 m. That is one eighth of a period after it left equilibrium.

items.q: Where is the block, and how is it moving, at t = 0?
options: At equilibrium, moving in the + direction at top speed
At x = +0.040 m, momentarily at rest
At equilibrium, momentarily at rest
At x = −0.040 m, moving in the + direction

why.correct: sin 0 = 0, so x = 0 at t = 0. Just after, sin is positive and growing, so the block moves in +x. At equilibrium its speed is at its largest.
options: Right: a sine graph starts at zero and rises.
That is how a cosine graph starts; this equation uses sine.
At equilibrium the block moves fastest; it is at rest only at the turning points.
sin 0 = 0, so the block is at x = 0, not at a turning point.

items.q: At t = 0.10 s, which describes the block?
options: At x = +0.040 m, with zero velocity and the largest acceleration, in −x
At x = 0, with the largest velocity and zero acceleration
At x = +0.040 m, with the largest velocity, in +x
At x = −0.040 m, with zero velocity and acceleration in +x

why.correct: 0.10 s is a quarter of the 0.40 s period: sin(2π × 2.5 × 0.10) = sin(π/2) = 1, so x = +0.040 m, a turning point. There v = 0, and the acceleration is largest and points toward equilibrium (−x).
options: Right: a quarter period after leaving equilibrium, the block is at +A.
x = 0 happens at t = 0 and 0.20 s, not at a quarter period.
At the turning point the block is momentarily at rest, not moving fastest.
The block reaches −0.040 m at three quarters of a period, t = 0.30 s.

items.q: Two identical blocks on identical springs are released from rest at the same moment, block 1 from 3.0 cm and block 2 from 6.0 cm. Which block returns to its release point first?
options: They return at the same time
Block 1, because it has a shorter distance to travel
Block 2, because it is pulled back by a larger force
Block 1, because its smaller force means less acceleration

why.correct: The period T = 2π√(m/k) is the same for both: block 2 travels twice as far but feels twice the force at each matching point, so it moves twice as fast. The two effects cancel.
options: Right: the period does not depend on the amplitude.
Block 1 does travel less distance, but it also moves more slowly; the times match.
Block 2 does feel a larger force, but it also has farther to go; the times match.
Less acceleration slows block 1 down, which works against it, not for it; the times still match.

items.q: For an object in simple harmonic motion, at which point is its speed zero and the size of its acceleration greatest?
options: At either turning point, x = ±A
At the equilibrium position, x = 0
Halfway between equilibrium and a turning point
At x = 0 for speed and x = ±A for acceleration

why.correct: At the turning points the object stops for an instant and the restoring force, −kx, has its largest size because |x| = A.
options: Right: speed zero and acceleration largest happen together, at the ends.
At x = 0 the speed is greatest and the acceleration is zero: the opposite.
At x = ±A/2 the object is still moving and the force is half its largest value.
At x = 0 the speed is largest, not zero.

items.q: A cart on a spring moves according to x = (0.12 m) cos(2π · 0.50 t). What is the first time after t = 0 at which the cart is at x = +0.060 m? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is a quarter of the period, when the cart reaches x = 0. Half the amplitude is reached sooner: solve cos(πt) = 0.5.
Value: you used the angle 60 in degrees as if it were radians. cos⁻¹(0.5) = π/3 rad.

why.correct: Set (0.12 m) cos(πt) = 0.060 m: cos(πt) = 0.5, so πt = π/3 and t = 1/3 s ≈ 0.33 s. The period is 2.0 s, so the cart covers the first half of its distance to equilibrium in one sixth of a period: it starts slowly.

items.q: A block on a spring is released from rest at x = +A at t = 0. Which equation describes its position?
options: x = A cos(2πft)
x = A sin(2πft)
x = −A cos(2πft)
x = A sin(2πft) + A

why.correct: At t = 0 the block must be at +A: cos 0 = 1 gives x = A. Both sine and cosine describe SHM; the starting point decides which one fits.
options: Right: cosine starts at its largest value.
This starts at x = 0, which fits a block that starts at equilibrium.
This starts at x = −A, the other turning point.
This oscillates between 0 and 2A, so its center is not the equilibrium position.

items.q: A block oscillates on a spring with amplitude A. It is stopped and set oscillating again with amplitude 2A. Predict how each quantity compares with the first motion.

variables.name: Largest speed
variables.why: The block covers twice the distance in the same time, so its top speed doubles.

variables.name: Largest acceleration
variables.why: The largest force is kA, so it doubles with A, and a = F/m doubles too.

why.correct: Amplitude scales the size of x, v and a, but the timing (period) is set by m and k alone.

items.q: The velocity of an object in SHM is graphed against time. At an instant when the velocity graph crosses zero going from positive to negative, where is the object?
options: At its largest positive displacement, x = +A
At its largest negative displacement, x = −A
At equilibrium, moving in the − direction
At equilibrium, moving in the + direction

why.correct: v = 0 means a turning point. Before that instant v was +, so the object was moving toward +x and has just reached the + end, x = +A.
options: Right: moving + and stopping means it has reached +A.
At −A the velocity changes from − to +, the opposite crossing.
At equilibrium the speed is largest, so v is not zero there.
At equilibrium v has its largest size, not zero.

items.q: A mass on a spring oscillates with amplitude 0.050 m and period 0.50 s. What is its largest speed? (Its speed is greatest at equilibrium and equals 2πA/T.) Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you divided the amplitude by the period with no 2π. In one period the object goes around a full cycle; its top speed is 2πA/T.
Value: 4A/T is the average speed over a cycle. The top speed, at equilibrium, is larger: 2πA/T.

why.correct: v_max = 2πA/T = 2π(0.050 m)/(0.50 s) = 0.63 m/s. The average speed is 4A/T = 0.40 m/s; the top speed is higher because the mass slows near the ends.
